 Petrol price drops 12.5% in six weeks; Pricey motorway stations down below €2.40/liter 
 Wednesday, 18 November 2026 - 18:40
 Petrol prices in the Netherlands are continuing to fall, with the recommended pump price dropping below €2.40 per liter, down about 12.5 percent since mid-October. Some petrol stations are already charging less than €2 per liter, offering motorists cheaper fuel than they have seen in months.
 UnitedConsumers reported that the average recommended price for Euro95 petrol dropped to €2.394 per liter on Wednesday, down by more than 1 cent from the previous day. The figure is calculated using prices set by the Netherlands' five largest oil companies. However, these recommended rates are mainly found at motorway stations, meaning motorists can often find cheaper fuel elsewhere.
 The average recommended price of petrol peaked at a record €2.732 per liter on October 10. It has been on a gradual downward trend ever since.
 Diesel prices followed a similar downward trend, slipping to €2.521 per liter on Wednesday, UnitedConsumers reported. The price has fallen since hitting an all-time high of €2.824 per liter on September 19.
 Motorists may see further reductions at the pump in the coming days as oil prices continue to fall. Lower crude prices often translate into cheaper fuel in the Netherlands after a delay. On Wednesday, Brent crude dropped 1.5 percent to nearly $92 a barrel, while U.S. crude fell 2 percent to just above $84.
 The Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz drove oil prices sharply higher earlier this year. However, Bloomberg reported that traders are now focusing less on renewed fighting in the Middle East and more on signs that oil supplies are recovering and stockpiles in the United States are increasing.
